title: I WILL GO DOWN WITH YOU

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I will go down to Egypt with you, and I will surely bring you back again. And Joseph's own hand will close your eyes.'" — Gen 46:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three promises, each one aimed at a fear.

"I will go down to Egypt with you." God does not send Jacob; God goes with him. This is the deepest comfort in all of Scripture — not that God directs our path from a distance, but that He walks it beside us. Whatever Egypt you are heading into, you will not enter it alone.

"I will surely bring you back again." Jacob himself would die in Egypt, but his body would be carried back to the family burial cave (Gen 50:13), and his descendants would return as a nation. God's promises are often bigger than one lifetime. He keeps them fully, but not always within the span we would have chosen.

"Joseph's own hand will close your eyes." What extraordinary tenderness. God tells an old man that when he dies, the son he grieved for twenty years will be right there beside him. God stoops to comfort Jacob about the smallest, most personal detail of his death.

Our God does not only handle nations and famines. He notices what an old man fears about his last day. He is that near, and He is nearer still in Christ, who promises to be with us always (Matt 28:20).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which of these three promises speaks most to your situation today?
2. Do you think of God as directing you from a distance, or walking beside you?
3. What small, personal fear could you bring to Him right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You do not just send me — You come with me. Thank You for caring about the smallest details of my life and my fears. Walk with me today. Amen.
